errors.text: Attributes disappearance of the smallest particles primarily to Ostwald ripening and predicts 2–3× growth, whereas the target mechanism emphasizes Au/Cu surface segregation followed by shell melting and evaporation, producing an approximately 22% reduction in average particle size.
Predicts Au/Pt surface enrichment with Cu in the core, but the target finds both Au and Cu segregating to the surface.
Predicts increasing faceting or anisotropy, whereas the observed evolution is predominantly an elliptical-to-spherical reshaping.
Places rapid loss within the first 100–200 K of heating without support; the experimentally relevant breakdown of sluggish behavior occurs around and above 673 K.
